name: Long-Term Residence (Non-EU/EEA Third-Country Nationals)

requirements.blocker_text: 5 years of continuous legal residence in Romania. Absences under 6 consecutive months (up to 10 months total) don't break continuity; study periods count at half value; temporary residence permits for studies, asylum-seeker status, short-stay visas, and seasonal/au-pair work do NOT qualify.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 5 years of continuous legal residence under a qualifying permit category.

requirements.blocker_text: Proof of financial means (waived for family members of Romanian citizens).
No removal order issued against the applicant; clean criminal record certificate required.

outcome.duration_length: 10 years if family member of a Romanian citizen; 5 years for other purposes
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: status ceases upon absence exceeding 12 consecutive months

sources.title: General Inspectorate for Immigration (IGI), Romanian Ministry of Internal Affairs -- long-term residence for non-EU/EEA citizens: 5 years' continuous legal residence (study periods count at half value; certain permit categories excluded), equal treatment with Romanian citizens on employment/education/social security/healthcare/tax/housing, 10-year permit for family of Romanian citizens or 5 years otherwise, status ends after 12 consecutive months' absence or on acquiring citizenship

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Romania). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- fully tier-1 IGI sourced. NAMING/STRUCTURAL NOTE: Romania runs two parallel tracks that both function as 'permanent residence' in ordinary usage but are legally and administratively distinct -- this file models 'long-term residence' (the track for non-EU/EEA third-country nationals, 5-year qualifying period, 5-10 year renewable card). A SEPARATE track, called 'permanent residence' in IGI's own terminology, exists only for EU/EEA/Swiss citizens and their family members exercising free-movement rights (also a 5-year qualifying period, but a 10-year card, per IGI's granting-permanent-residence page) -- that EU-citizen-specific track is not modeled as its own file here, consistent with this dataset's focus on third-country-national routes, but the naming overlap is flagged so it isn't mistaken for a duplicate or an error. citizenship_after_months is set to 36, representing the ADDITIONAL months of continuous residence needed after reaching this long-term-residence status (60 months) to reach naturalisation's 8-year/96-month total continuous-residence requirement under Article 8(1)(a) -- see ro_citizenship_naturalisation.json for that authoritative total. This is an arithmetic inference (96 minus 60), not a figure IGI states directly for long-term-residence holders.
